sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Lady of the Lake is an Arthurian heroine, also called Dame du Lac. Sometimes she is named Nimue or Morgause, though she is set apart from those characters. She gives the king-to-be Arthur the magical sword Excalibur. In the early texts she is a fairy who lives in the Celtic otherworld. Her realm is the Land of Women, called Tir na mBan. She dwells on a magical lake ringed by her maiden servants. She captures Lancelot and brings him up to serve as her protector. For this he is called Lancelot of the Lake. In some sources Lancelot is her lover and the father of the pure knight Galahad. Later texts lower the fairy queen to a mere sorceress who builds an illusory lake. Her power in the Arthurian tales stays firm, since she guards Arthur for his whole life. At the end he gives back Excalibur to the lake and the Lady conveys him away. Scholars compare her bond with Arthur to that of the goddess Mórrígan and the hero Cúchulainn.

okr.objective: Document Dame du Lac, the Lady of the Lake who gives Arthur the sword Excalibur.
